notes: Houhanshu 38 s0283-s0289, Houhanshu 115 s0026-s0027 and Houhanshu 116 s0025-s0026 all describe Minister of Works 司空周章 plotting to depose Empress Dowager Deng and enthrone Liu Sheng, and dying when the plot was discovered.

Hanshu 1 s0091 陳涉之將周章 is Chen She's general of 209 BC; Houhanshu 38 p118 is the Eastern Han Minister of Works active AD 92-107. The prior model merges (cohort-2026-08-27-01 #949, prompt-v7-batch-2026-08-12-continuation-50d #193) rested on the shared name 周章 alone.
Liu Bang's second elder brother 仲 (喜), made King of Dai in 201 BC and demoted to Marquis of Heyang: Shiji 50 s0009, Hanshu 2 s0127/s0157, Hanshu 3 s0031.

Houhanshu 38 s0144-s0145 太尉東萊劉喜 is the Eastern Han Grand Commandant of AD 125, dismissed at Emperor Shun's accession; he cannot be the King of Dai of 201 BC. The prior model merge cohort-2026-08-27-01 #892 rested on the shared name 劉喜 alone.
Houhanshu 38 s0098 吳起與田文論功…田文相魏 retells Shiji 65 s0116-s0130 魏置相，相田文 and Wu Qi's merit debate with him.

Liangshu 14 s0262 類田文之愛客 alludes to Lord Mengchang 孟嘗君 of Qi, the patron of retainers, active about 300-279 BC; Wu Qi's rival chancellor of Wei served before Wu Qi died in 381 BC. The prior model merges (cohort-2026-08-27-01 #67, prompt-v7-batch-2026-08-13-continuation-50j #5501) conflated the two Tian Wen.
